owners.subject: chronik: V2 index bounds follow the consensus block-size limit
owners.message:
chronik: V2 index bounds follow the consensus block-size limit

The V2 index skipped connect_block for valid large blocks ("Chronik V2
connect_block skipped: invalid V2 index transition: staging capacity"),
and the V2 service then stayed not ready. Its fixed bounds were 4096
transactions, 65536 changes and 32 MiB of reserved staging per block, far
below the consensus block-size limit: a single regtest transaction
spending 1500 outputs (70 KB) already exceeded the staging reservation.

The bounds now derive from the consensus block-size limit (`Bounds`): the
most transactions (58-byte shortest transaction), created plus consumed
outputs (42-byte shortest input) and staged bytes that a block within the
limit can produce. Every per-element staging reservation, charged to the
shortest wire encoding of its element, stays within 1024 reserved bytes
per wire byte (the worst case is a spend, about 770 bytes per byte), plus
64 KiB per block; staging_covers_shortest_encodings checks this. So any
valid block is indexed, and the reservation stays an early, explicit cap
rather than unbounded allocation. Memory of one connect is linear in the
block's size, as it is for the node; at the 1 GB adaptive ceiling the
reservation bound is large, but real blocks reserve only for what they
contain.

The host passes the limit as ServiceLimits.block_bytes: the configured
maximum block size, at least the adaptive ceiling (1 GB), within 32 bits
(get_v2_max_block_bytes). The service checks a block's wire bytes against
it and its copied facts against the derived staging bound; transaction and
change limits above what such a block can hold are refused. The stored
records and receipts are unchanged.

Chunking a block across several write transactions was not chosen: it
would need a schema for partial blocks and their crash recovery, while the
derived bound keeps one atomic commit per block.

Tests: block_over_former_fixed_bounds_is_indexed connects and disconnects
a 4100-transaction block whose reservation exceeds 32 MiB; the capacity
and transaction-bound tests use small explicit bounds; the service
boundary test checks block_bytes against a header-only block.

owners.subject: chronik(v2): index points into the node's block files instead of copying txs
owners.message:
chronik(v2): index points into the node's block files instead of copying txs

The V2 index (Rust chronik-db and native lotus_v2, kept at byte parity)
no longer copies transactions. A tx record stores the transaction's
block-file position; bytes are read back through the node and checked
against the recorded identity, size and checksum.

Records (schema 4, identical postcard layouts in Rust and native):
- eT TxMeta: location, lock, counts, file_num u32, data_pos u32 (was
  u64 into v2_tx_NNNNN.dat), wire_size, wire_checksum (seahash).
- 'b' receipt: (anchor, parent, block facts, [ReceiptTx {location,
  file_num, data_pos, wire_size, wire_checksum}]) instead of full txs.
- coins subdb (was outputs; key 'o'+outpoint): Coin {flags, value,
  token_id iff flags&1, spend: Option<(spender txid, input index)>}.
  The script/branches/paths and the creation location are no longer
  copied; queries that need them read the creating tx through the node.
- eI stores StoredInputMeta without the frozen spent output; the
  public InputMeta.resolved_creation is filled at query time.
- Undo drops the flat-file position.
- The flat files (v2_tx_*.dat) and the outputs table are gone.

Reading: a TxSource (node: ChronikBridge::read_tx_from_disk /
ReadTxFromDisk, under the block's own BridgeV2NativeTx conversion;
tests: MemTxSource) loads NodeTx at (file, pos); the index checks txid,
txhash, wire size and seahash and fails closed (Error::Node / Corrupt).
Positions are bindex.nDataPos + header + CompactSize(vtx), advanced by
each tx's serialized size, read under cs_main. Read budgets are
unchanged. Connect resolves spent coins from in-block creations or the
coin record; exact replay compares receipt, explorer entries, coins and
spend refs. Disconnect rebuilds the block from the node and verifies the
undo exactly.

Schema: SCHEMA_VERSION 3 -> 4. An older index is refused on open with
"V2 index schema version 3 is incompatible with version 4; restart with
-chronikreindex to rebuild the V2 index" (Rust Error::Schema, native
V2Error::Schema / V2SchemaError); hosts do not wipe on this error.

leave the index untouched; -chronikreindex rebuilds it (tip 202) and the
old v2_tx_00000.dat is gone.

owners.message:
[v2 only] net: P2P over WebSocket only, on the P2P port

Lotus v2 has no raw TCP P2P. Measured on loopback, WebSocket adds about
5 us to a P2P round trip (zstd 18 us, TLS another 28 us), and blocks sync
as fast as over TCP; on real networks that is noise.

- Listening: the P2P binds (-bind, -whitebind, onion binds, the default
  any-address binds) open HTTP/WebSocket listeners on the HTTP server,
  with TLS detected per connection. Inbound peers arrive through
  /p2p/ws; -whitebind permissions are applied by the listener reached,
  and onion peers are recognized by their bind as before. The raw
  listening sockets, their accept path and BindListenPort are gone.

owners.subject: [v2 only] net: p2p-v2 WebSocket framing
owners.message:
[v2 only] net: p2p-v2 WebSocket framing

Lotus v2 peers speak a single WebSocket subprotocol, p2p-v2, and drop the
v1 message header inside it:

- Each P2P message is one WebSocket message: a 1-byte message id (or 0,
  a length byte and the name, for types without an id), then the
  payload. The WebSocket message carries the length. There is no network
  magic and no checksum: TLS, Tor or the private network, and WebSocket
  framing already delimit and protect each message.
- Messages of 64 bytes or more are compressed with the connection's zstd
  stream and the built-in dictionary, and marked by RSV1 on the first
  frame. Smaller ones are sent plain.
- Ids index g_p2p_v2_message_types in src/protocol.cpp, which is
  append-only: new message types are added at the end and never
  renumbered.

The node offers and accepts only p2p-v2 (other upgrades get HTTP 400;
-p2pwebsocketoffer is ignored with a log line). P2PV2TransportDeserializer
rejects empty and oversized messages, and names longer than the message.
Oversized messages log the same "Header error: Size too large" line as v1.
getpeerinfo reports the compression as "p2p-v2", and bytes*_per_msg counts
5 bytes per message (length and id) instead of 24.

The test framework converts its v1 messages to and from p2p-v2
(ws_transport.P2PV2Converter). p2p.p2p_msg_overhead() gives the
per-message header size for byte-count checks. Tests that exercise v1
framing errors (magic, checksum, header) run only with
TEST_P2P_TRANSPORT=tcp.

Consolidated-stack adaptation: retain the native payload-limit includes;
append 16 compact command ids after the original 41 in matching C++/Python
tables; derive the IBD byte oracle from native block serializations and
transport overhead. The unknown-name test uses an unassigned custom name.

owners.subject: v2: add the xpi1 address format (encoder, decoder, spec, vectors)
owners.message:
v2: add the xpi1 address format (encoder, decoder, spec, vectors)

Lotus V2 outputs lock coins to branch roots, so a V2 address carries one
32-byte root rather than a script or hash type. Add the format and its
codec; wiring it into key_io, RPC, the wallet and Chronik is separate
work, and cashaddr stays in place until then.

Format (doc/standards/xpiaddr.md):

  <hrp> "1" <version> <52 payload symbols> <8 checksum symbols>

- hrp "xpi" (mainnet), "txpi" (testnet), "rxpi" (regtest); always
  required. "1" keeps the whole address double-click selectable.
- Version symbol 0 = one branch root; other versions are rejected.
- Payload: the root's 256 bits, high bit first, plus 4 zero padding bits.
- Checksum: cashaddr's 40-bit BCH PolyMod over the 61 body symbols,
  equal to a per-network constant (0xb70061479e, 0xadda0f1635,
  0x8172b45d63). The prefix is not expanded into the checksum; the
  constant binds the network.
- Lowercase on output; all-uppercase accepted for QR codes; mixed case
  rejected; no error correction. 65 characters on mainnet.

This keeps cashaddr's alphabet and checksum strength but drops the parts
that implementations got wrong: prefix expansion, the size-coded version
byte, variable-length regrouping and the optional prefix.

The constants were chosen so that no pattern of up to four character
substitutions turns an address on one network into a valid address on
another. Constants derived directly from the chain ids did not have this
property: a testnet address with four characters changed could decode
as a valid mainnet address.

Detection: any burst of up to 8 symbols, any single insertion or
deletion, any wrong-network string with up to 4 substitutions; at least
5 substitutions on one network (verified exhaustively; cashaddr's design
claims 6 within 126 symbols).

- src/lotus_v2/address.{h,cpp}: C++ codec with stable rejection reasons.
- src/test/data/lotus_v2_address.json: 13 valid and 30 invalid vectors,
  each invalid one with its exact reason.
- lotus_v2_address_tests: vectors plus encode/decode round trips.
- test_framework/xpiaddr.py: Python reference; its self-test checks the
  same vectors and runs with the framework unit tests.

owners.subject: v2: add EXT2 two-byte opcode framing and a 16-bit opcode IR
owners.message:
v2: add EXT2 two-byte opcode framing and a 16-bit opcode IR

P03 reserves 0xff (EXT2) as a prefix for 256 two-byte opcodes `ff xx`
(encoding candidate B, chosen on 2026-10-19). Until now the VM treated
0xff as one more unassigned byte, so `ff 4c` succeeded only by accident
and a trailing lone `ff` also succeeded.

- The decoded instruction opcode is now a 16-bit VmOpcode: a single
  byte b is 0x00bb and `ff xx` is 0xff00|xx. 0x00ff never executes.
- Scan: at 0xff a selector byte is required (a lone trailing prefix is
  "truncated EXT2", Invalid, even after RETURN or in a skipped arm). An
  unassigned pair returns invocation success; no pair is assigned at
  genesis, so every `ff xx` is OP_SUCCESS_EXT_xx. The selector is never
  parsed as a push or as a one-byte opcode.
- VmCostProfile gains an ext_opcode table indexed by selector. OpCost
  and the static size pass take a VmOpcode; CheckCostProfile requires a
  positive base for every assigned two-byte opcode (none yet). The
  ordinary-validation profile digest covers the new table.

field_sizes keys stay uint8_t: only one-byte opcodes take field-size
hints, and the key can widen when a two-byte opcode needs one.

Tests: all 256 `ff xx` pairs succeed; lone/trailing `ff` rejects; push
payload ff is data; a malformed push before the prefix still rejects;
structural-only charge. The fuzz target asserts the same scan rules.

owners.subject: v2: sync the VM opcode allocation with the P03 registry
owners.message:
v2: sync the VM opcode allocation with the P03 registry

The VM's genesis allocation (215 bytes) predates the current P03
registry (docs/lotus-v2/tools/opcodes.json at lotus-v2-optimizations
2db77639, sha256 aa337a17...b014), which assigns 225 bytes. V2 has no
live genesis, so this is a pre-genesis reallocation, not a soft fork;
fixtures and dev chains that relied on the old bytes must be
regenerated.

- 0x67/0x68 (fused input/output loop headers) are retired to
  OP_SUCCESS_103/104. Loops now come only from ENUMERATE (0x69); the
  fused-loop decode, execution and size-pass code is removed. Use
  `TXINPUTCOUNT ENUMERATE` / `TXOUTPUTCOUNT ENUMERATE` instead.
- 0x6c (EMITLOG) is assigned and permanently invalid on-chain. The scan
  rejects as soon as it reaches 0x6c, so a later success byte, a skipped
  arm or an earlier RETURN cannot hide it (decision I-3). A success byte
  scanned before it still wins, and a 6c inside push data is data.
- STATEHASH c3, UTXOFLAGS de, INPUTWITNESSARG df, ENFORCEOUTPUT eb,
  TXTOKENBALANCE ec, STATEVERIFY ed, UTXOSTATEROOT ee, OUTPUTSTATEROOT
  ef, ACTIVEBRANCHINDEX f5 and ACTIVEWITNESSINDEX f6 are assigned. Until
  their semantics land they are Unsupported, never success.
- 0xff is counted as assigned (EXT2 prefix, previous commit).
- Cost profiles must price every executable assigned byte; EMITLOG and
  the EXT2 prefix need no one-byte cost.

vm_test/opcode_coverage.json now lists the 225 registry entries with a
status (push, control, implemented, unsupported, invalid, prefix) and
the new registry digest; check_opcode_coverage.py checks it against the
registry and the native dispatch. test_vm checks every single byte
against the registry's 31 success bytes, the 67/68 retirement, EMITLOG
in every scan position, and Unsupported for the new bytes. Fused-loop
vectors in test_vm and the Python differentials are rewritten with
`TXINPUTCOUNT ENUMERATE`; the external Python reference VM must be
updated separately.

owners.subject: v2: cap V2 transactions at 256 inputs and 256 outputs
owners.message:
v2: cap V2 transactions at 256 inputs and 256 outputs

The V2 wire format counts inputs and outputs with u16, and the code
accepted up to 65,535 of each (the default profile used that bound).
ENUMERATE takes a bound of 0..256, so a covenant written as
`TXINPUTCOUNT ENUMERATE ... ENDENUMERATE` would error on a larger
transaction, and with partial-mode signatures a third party could add
inputs or outputs to make such a covenant unspendable (I-6).

Decision (2026-10-19): V2 consensus caps inputs and outputs at 256
each, so the ENUMERATE idiom always covers the whole transaction. The
65,535 in the encoding spec remains the wire-format bound only.

- lotus_v2/transaction.h: MAX_TX_INPUTS / MAX_TX_OUTPUTS = 256;
  DefaultTxProfile uses them (mints share the input cap).
- Transaction codec and ordinary-validation profiles may only tighten
  the caps; a looser profile is rejected.
- consensus/tx_check.cpp: nVersion 7 transactions (including V2
  coinbases) with more than 256 inputs or outputs are rejected with
  bad-txns-v2-too-many-inputs / -outputs. MAX_V2_TX_* in
  consensus/consensus.h is static_asserted equal to the V2 constants.
- Test runners and fixtures that used 65,535 now use 256.
- Transaction identity never depends on the caps.
  ComputeTransactionIdentities bounds counts only by the u16 wire format
  (MAX_WIRE_TX_INPUTS / MAX_WIRE_TX_OUTPUTS = 65,535) and ignores the
  profile's max_inputs/max_outputs/max_mints, so a transaction over the
  cap keeps the TxId of its bytes and is rejected by validation, rather
  than silently receiving the flat fallback digest.
- A transaction that is not a well-formed V2 transaction still gets the
  flat fallback digest (it must be nameable for logs and reject caches),
  but CTransaction records this (HasStructuralV2Identity) and
  CheckRegularTransaction / CheckCoinbase reject it with
  bad-txns-v2-identity after every more specific rule. This catches, for
  example, a legacy-version transaction with more than 65,535 outputs.

Tests: encode/decode at exactly 256 outputs, rejection at 257 (encode,
and decode of a wire whose u16 count says 257), looser codec and
ordinary profiles rejected, CheckRegularTransaction at 256/257; a
257-output transaction's TxId/TxHash/outputs root equal those computed
from its serialized bytes and survive a round trip, and validation
rejects it with bad-txns-v2-too-many-outputs; a legacy transaction with
65,535 outputs keeps a structural identity and one with 65,536 is
rejected with bad-txns-v2-identity.

The mempool admission helper publishes at most 256 outputs per
confirmed transaction. A larger wallet is funded by chained P2PK change
from the one mature coinbase, one transaction per block. The cap is
unchanged.

owners.subject: v2: bound TXINPUTCOUNT/TXOUTPUTCOUNT ENUMERATE by the actual count
owners.message:
v2: bound TXINPUTCOUNT/TXOUTPUTCOUNT ENUMERATE by the actual count

With the fused 67/68 loop headers retired, a loop over inputs or
outputs is written `TXINPUTCOUNT ENUMERATE ... ENDENUMERATE` (or with
TXOUTPUTCOUNT). The size pass only knew literal bounds, so it charged
such a loop at 256 iterations (65,536 when nested), a large regression
from the fused headers, which were charged at the exact count (I-7).

Decision (2026-10-19): when the instruction immediately before
ENUMERATE in the same sequence is TXINPUTCOUNT or TXOUTPUTCOUNT, the
static bound is min(256, count), taken from the counts the invocation
is charged with (the transaction's own counts with a context).
Otherwise a literal bound is used, otherwise 256. Execution is
unchanged: the popped bound must be 0..256, which the 256 input/output
cap now guarantees for real transactions.

Tests: at 0, 1, 2, 255 and 256 inputs the idiom charges exactly what a
one-byte constant bound charges, 16 less than a 16-byte literal, the
old fused-header charge plus 34, and equals its executed cost; 257 is
charged as 256 and errors at run time; the nested input/output idiom
equals nested constants; an instruction between the count and
ENUMERATE loses the precision; three nested loops never decode.

owners.subject: v2: make BREAK conditional (Boolean(cond) N(depth) BREAK)
owners.message:
v2: make BREAK conditional (Boolean(cond) N(depth) BREAK)

P03 now defines BREAK as `Boolean(cond) N(depth) -> empty`: N(1) exits
`depth` enclosing loops, N(0) continues, so a loop exit no longer needs
an IF ... ENDIF wrapper and an unconditional break is `ONE <depth>
BREAK`. The VM still popped only the depth and always exited.

- Execution pops N(depth) then the condition, checks
  1 <= depth <= active loops before acting on the condition (so a bad
  depth errors even with cond N(0)), requires a canonical Boolean, and
  either returns ExitLoops(depth) or continues. BREAK in a skipped arm
  or a zero-iteration loop still does not execute.
- The size pass pops both operands, charges them at their abstract
  sizes (the old pass charged the depth at 16 bytes even when a wider
  numeric could be supplied), records the exit states as before and
  continues with the fall-through state instead of ending the sequence.

Tests: cond 0 runs every iteration, cond 1 exits and skips the rest of
the body, depth 2 with both conditions, out-of-range depth with cond 0,
non-Boolean and 17-byte conditions, underflow, skipped arms; the static
charge equals the executed charge for a fall-through body and bounds it
for a taken BREAK and for wide operands. Existing vectors and the
Python differential cases are rewritten to the new operand order.

owners.subject: v2: add HAS_STATE outputs with a 32-byte state root
owners.message:
v2: add HAS_STATE outputs with a 32-byte state root

Output flag bit 2 (HAS_STATE) adds a 32-byte state_root to a V2 output.
The wire order is flags | value | token_id? | state_root? | branches |
paths, so OutputLeaf, OutputsRoot, TxID, TxHash, CoinEntry and the
sighash commitments all cover the root through the shared EncodeOutput.

Rules (plan I-8, I-9):
- flags & 0xf8 is invalid; HAS_STATE together with IS_BURN (0x06, 0x07)
  is invalid; HAS_STATE requires a nonzero root and a nonzero root
  requires the flag.
- A coinbase may not create a HAS_STATE output, since it runs no script
  and could never authorize state: the lotus_v2 coinbase-shape rule, the
  v7 wire decoder and CheckCoinbase ("bad-cb-state-output") reject it.
- Interim until transaction-scoped VM effects land: ordinary validation
  and the daemon script checks reject every HAS_STATE output with
  "state-output-unauthorized", so no unauthorized state exists mid-stack.

MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES grows from 812 to 844. CTxOut gains stateRoot, carried
through SetNull, operator==, To/FromV2Output, the legacy adapter, the
coinbase builders and the v7 (de)serializer. The coins compressor V2 tag
range widens from kV2TagBase..+3 to +7 and stores the root, fixing the
silent loss of the HAS_STATE bit (plan risk 3); this is a coins-DB format
change for the structured form. RPC decoderawtransaction,
getrawtransaction and gettxout show "stateRoot" when present.

Deviation: MAX_COIN_BYTES stays 10068 because internal legacy state
coins already dominate it; the test now checks the V2 maxima directly
(868 bytes stateless, 900 with a root), which also repairs the
test_sparse_state assertion that failed on the base commit.
coins_resource_is_used now inserts as many nodes as fit in one pool
chunk, because the larger CTxOut no longer fits 1000.

owners.subject: v2: implement UTXOFLAGS, UTXOSTATEROOT, OUTPUTSTATEROOT and active indexes
owners.message:
v2: implement UTXOFLAGS, UTXOSTATEROOT, OUTPUTSTATEROOT and active indexes

Five registered context readers move from Unsupported to implemented:

- de UTXOFLAGS (i -> N): flags of the spent coin at input i. Like the
  other UTXO readers it requires a spend input with a resolved coin, so
  a mint (or out-of-range index) is an error.
- ee UTXOSTATEROOT (i -> Hash32): the spent coin's state_root, or 32
  zero bytes when the coin lacks HAS_STATE.
- ef OUTPUTSTATEROOT (j -> Hash32): output j's state_root, or zeros.
- f5 ACTIVEBRANCHINDEX (-> N): coin.paths[path_index][witness_index] for
  a spend; N(-1) for a mint, which has no branch.
- f6 ACTIVEWITNESSINDEX (-> N): the witness index; N(0) for a mint
  (plan I-16).

All require an authenticated context (Unsupported without one). The
static size pass gives exact 16-byte (de, f5, f6) and 32-byte (ee, ef)
results, so static accounting equals the executed cost. The opcode
coverage inventory marks the five bytes implemented.

owners.subject: v2: implement TXTOKENBALANCE over prepared per-asset totals
owners.message:
v2: implement TXTOKENBALANCE over prepared per-asset totals

ec TXTOKENBALANCE pops a 32-byte asset id and pushes N(inputs) then
N(outputs) for that asset across the whole transaction. The zero id
selects the native asset. Spent coins count as inputs (a mint input
contributes nothing, so for a minted token out - in is the mint delta);
every output, burns included, counts as an output. An asset that does
not appear yields 0 0, and an operand that is not exactly 32 bytes is an
error. The opcode requires an authenticated context.

The totals are computed once per transaction: PreparedVmTransaction
stores them at preparation, and a context without a prepared snapshot
computes them lazily once per invocation. The accumulation rule
(AddVmAssetTotal) is now shared with ordinary validation, which keeps
its native/token split by reading and removing the zero key, so the
opcode and the conservation checks cannot disagree.

owners.subject: v2: implement INPUTWITNESSARG for any input's witness arguments
owners.message:
v2: implement INPUTWITNESSARG for any input's witness arguments

df INPUTWITNESSARG pops i w a and pushes argument a of witness w of
input i. Per decision I-12 it may read any input, not only the running
invocation, so a script can inspect sibling witnesses and other inputs.
Bounds per input kind: a spend has one witness per path slot
(w < len(witnesses)); a mint has exactly witness 0; a coinbase input has
none and errors. Every out-of-range index is an introspection error. The
result is bounded by the element cap like any push.

For the static size pass, PreparedVmTransaction records the widest
witness argument in the transaction, so the charged cost uses that
bound instead of the element cap; without a prepared snapshot the cap is
used. Deviation from plan 4.x: this is a prepared maximum rather than a
new 0xdf field_sizes vector, which keeps caller cost profiles unchanged.

The VS:236 spec text amendment for I-12 is outside this tree.

owners.subject: v2: implement STATEHASH and STATEVERIFY with a contractstate tag
owners.message:
v2: implement STATEHASH and STATEVERIFY with a contractstate tag

c3 STATEHASH pops N(k) and then k items (item_1 deepest) and pushes
TaggedHash("Lotus/v2/contractstate", CS(k) || for each item CS(len) ||
item) with shortest-form CompactSize. k must be 0..64 and the stack must
hold the items. Per decision I-13 the digest uses its own domain tag,
HashDomain::ContractState, rather than the block StateRoot's
"Lotus/v2/state". ContractStateHash streams the preimage into BLAKE3
without building it. The opcode is context-free.

ed STATEVERIFY pops a 32-byte root and requires the running invocation
to be a spend whose coin has HAS_STATE and exactly that state_root; a
mint, a coin without state, a wrong width or a mismatch is an error.

Costs: STATEHASH charges per_operand_byte over the items, the count and
the CompactSize framing (so the charge covers the whole preimage). The
size pass uses the literal count when the preceding instruction is a
numeric push, else the 64-item worst case (WorstOpCost now covers 65
operands plus framing for c3). With a literal count, static accounting
equals the executed cost.

Digest vectors for k = 0, 1, 2, 3 and 64 come from the Python reference
in test_framework.messages; native tests also check streaming against
the materialized tagged hash for 300- and 2000-byte items.

owners.subject: v2: add transaction-scoped VM effects and a per-transaction post-check
owners.message:
v2: add transaction-scoped VM effects and a per-transaction post-check

Per decision I-11, effects are order-free. VmTransactionEffects collects
the (output, claim) pairs and the state authorizations recorded by a
transaction's successful invocations; nothing consumes a shared budget
during execution, so invocations may run in any order. Each invocation
stages its effects in the machine and EvaluateVm commits them to
context.effects only on Success (AutomaticSuccess and failures commit
nothing), the same pattern as staged signatures. The accumulator is
owned by one validation run and is never stored in PreparedVmTransaction,
which tl_cache reuses across checks.

FinalizeVmTransactionEffects runs once per transaction after every
invocation succeeded: the claims on output j must sum to at most
outputs[j].value ("output-overclaimed") and every HAS_STATE output must
have been authorized ("state-output-unauthorized"). It replaces the
interim HAS_STATE rejects from the HAS_STATE patch in:

- ordinary validation, after the input-ascending/witness-ascending loop;
- CheckInputScripts, which now treats a V2 transaction as one check
  unit (its inputs are never deferred to pvChecks) and finalizes before
  writing the script-execution cache;
- VerifyTxScriptsFromResolvedCoins, including its OP_TRUE/CHECKSIG fast
  path, so the shortcut cannot bypass the post-check.

No opcode produces effects yet (ENFORCEOUTPUT follows), so every
HAS_STATE output is still rejected, now by the post-check.

owners.subject: v2: implement ENFORCEOUTPUT with order-free output claims
owners.message:
v2: implement ENFORCEOUTPUT with order-free output claims

ENFORCEOUTPUT (0xeb) pops a claim and an OutputTemplate, plus any
template-directed stack operands (value, stack-pinned branch roots in
descending slot order, a state root, an output index). It selects the
first output that matches the template and stages (j, claim), plus j as a
state-authorized output when the template constrains state. It pushes j.
Staged effects commit only when the invocation succeeds. The
per-transaction post-check from the previous patch then requires the sum
of claims on each output not to exceed its value, and every HAS_STATE
output to be authorized.

Following decision I-11, claims do not consume a running budget, and the
search ignores budgets. Two identical templates therefore select the same
output and are judged by their sum, and greedy-order failures cannot
occur.

The template format and its parser are in output_template.h. Matching
covers:
- value: EXACT, MIN, FROM_STACK
- token: NATIVE, EXACT (a zero id means native), SELF (the active branch
  root, or the minted token id)
- branch count and pins
- paths: OMIT (pinned roots must be required on every path), EXPLICIT,
  INHERIT (rejected in mints)
- the burn and wildcard flags
- state: NONE (excludes HAS_STATE outputs), TEMPLATE, STACK

Each scanned output costs per_scanned_output. A literal template pushed
directly before the claim gets an exact static charge. Any other form is
charged the worst case.

Deviations from the plan:
- The template gains an output_mode byte (first match, index in the
  template, index from the stack). Under I-11, "a script that needs a
  specific output pins it", and this is the explicit pin.
- The parser is header-only, so every VM target gets it without
  build-file changes.
- per_scanned_output is a new VmOpcodeCost field. CheckCostProfile does
  not require it to be nonzero, because that would invalidate every
  existing profile. It is part of the ordinary profile digest, but not of
  block-transition serialization, so fixture hashes are unchanged.
- A burn template with OMIT paths compares pins by slot only, because
  burns carry no paths.

Tests: an EnforceOutput matrix over a fixed 4-output transaction:
- every mode
- pop order with three stack roots
- template and stack output pinning
- malformed templates: every truncation length, trailing bytes, modes,
  mask overlap/range, zero state, burn with paths
- claim range, and Unsupported without an effects accumulator
- discarded effects on failure
- N-to-1 and over-claim post-checks, and a pinned repair
- an I-10 zero-claim state authorizer
- exact versus worst-case static cost
- a self-continuing vault

owners.subject: v2: add a non-consensus simulation evaluator
owners.message:
v2: add a non-consensus simulation evaluator

EvaluateVmSimulated (vm_simulation.h) runs every invocation of a draft
transaction in consensus order. The draft may have no outputs and unsigned
witnesses. The evaluator is for wallets, compilers and the RPC layer. It
reuses the consensus Machine through a hooks pointer that only
vm_simulation.cpp supplies. The consensus entrypoints in vm.h cannot set
it, and still reject 0x6c at scan time.

In simulation, following plan section 4.9:
- EMITLOG pops N(k), k in 0..64, then k items, and records
  {input, witness, instruction index, items}. The topic is the top item.
- ENFORCEOUTPUT first matches strictly over current outputs, including
  earlier drafts. This is the coalescing.
- Otherwise, unless the template pins an output index, ENFORCEOUTPUT
  appends a draft built from the template:
  - value: EXACT or FROM_STACK value, MIN's template value, OMIT's claim
  - token: by mode, with SELF giving the active root or minted id
  - branches: pinned roots; INHERIT without wildcard copies the coin
  - other slots: placeholder H("Lotus/v2/sim/placeholder",
    u16 output || u8 slot), flagged wallet_fill_required
  - paths: explicit, inherited, or one path over every slot; none for
    burns
  - state: the expected root
- Each draft records its template bytes, popped operands, claim, and any
  preceding "lotus.output.draft" event.
- With SimSignatures::AssumeValid, CHECKSIG/CHECKSIGVERIFY with correct
  framing and a valid key pass, as does CHECKDATASIG with a nonempty
  signature. Each records a signing request with the message it must
  cover.
- The result is flagged provisional when drafts were appended, or when a
  mint had no positive delta yet and was given 1. The per-transaction
  post-check is reported, not enforced.
- A failed invocation keeps its events but drops its drafts and signing
  requests, as its effects are dropped.

Deviations from the plan:
- An event records the instruction index rather than a byte offset.
  Instructions carry no offsets.
- Simulation runs with unit execution costs and no static charge.
- The provisional mint delta of 1 is this patch's answer for a mint whose
  token outputs do not exist yet. Plan section 4.9 does not cover it.

Tests (test_lotus_v2_vm_simulation):
- consensus rejects 6c while simulation accepts it; k bounds; item order
- zero-output drafts; coalescing with a reported over-claim, and MIN
  merging
- an existing match appends no draft
- placeholders, burn, and an INHERIT stateful continuation
- a pinned index is not constructed; draft-event linkage
- a failed invocation leaves no draft
- a mint creating its own token output, then re-simulation of the
  completed draft
- assumed signatures and signing requests, with framing still checked

The opcode coverage checker accepts the simulation-only 6c dispatch case.

owners.subject: v2: reject HAS_STATE outputs in non-v7 transactions
owners.message:
v2: reject HAS_STATE outputs in non-v7 transactions

Only a V2 script can authorize a HAS_STATE output: ENFORCEOUTPUT with a
state-constraining template, checked by the per-transaction post-check.
That post-check runs only for v7 transactions. A transaction of any other
version could therefore create a stateful output, with an arbitrary
"authenticated" root, through the legacy scriptPubKey output bridge.
CheckTransactionCommon now rejects such outputs with
bad-txns-legacy-state-output. Coinbases are covered too.

The check decodes only outputs whose first wire byte (or native flags)
has the state bit and no unknown bits. Ordinary scripts are not decoded.

Test: transaction_tests/v2_legacy_state_output. A legacy transaction
with a stateful bridge output is rejected. The same output without state,
and a P2PKH output, are accepted.

owners.subject: v2: add V2 VM profile, test and simulate RPCs
owners.message:
v2: add V2 VM profile, test and simulate RPCs

New RPCs (rpc/v2vm.cpp), following plan section 4.10:
- getv2vmprofile reports, for compilers and wallets:
  - the class of every single-byte opcode (success, assigned,
    simulation-only, ext2-prefix) and the assigned EXT2 selectors
  - the opcodes.json SHA-256
  - the node VmProfile and cost schedule
  - VmProfileDigest, a non-consensus commitment over both (tag
    "Lotus/v2/vmprofile")
  - the input/output, ENUMERATE, STATEHASH, EMITLOG and output-shape
    limits
- testv2transaction evaluates every invocation of a v7 transaction
  against the tip and mempool coins, without changing node state. For
  each invocation it reports the status, error, accounting and executed
  cost, and its claims and state authorizations. It then reports the
  per-transaction post-check with each output's claimed and unclaimed
  value.
- simulatev2transaction runs EvaluateVmSimulated over a draft, which may
  have zero outputs and no signatures. It returns the completed draft hex,
  events, drafts, signing requests (assume_valid_signatures), the
  provisional flag and the reported post-check. It requires

owners.subject: v2: name non-structural transactions by their complete serialization
owners.message:
v2: name non-structural transactions by their complete serialization

A transaction that is not a well-formed V2 structure (for example one
that spends an outpoint twice, or a legacy-version transaction with more
than 65,535 outputs) has no structural TxId. ComputeV2TxIdentities then
fell back to a flat hash that omitted the path index, every witness
after the first, siblings and arguments, concatenated variable-length
fields without length prefixes, silently skipped outputs that failed to
encode, and reused the TxId/TxHash tags without the chain ID. Two
different transactions could therefore share a name, and an invalid
transaction could be named like a valid one on another chain. Such
transactions are rejected, but rejection is recorded by name, so a
collision could poison a reject-cache entry for a different transaction.

The fallback now hashes, under its own domain tag
"Lotus/v2/txid/nonstructural", the active chain ID followed by the
complete serialized transaction. The serialization is self-delimiting
and is what the node relays, so distinct transactions get distinct
names, and the tag keeps them apart from every structural TxId and
TxHash. A non-structural transaction has no witness-free core, so its
TxId and TxHash are the same value. The test framework's mirror in
lotus_v2_compute_tx_identities (introduced by v2/034) computes the same
name.

transaction_tests checks that variants differing only in path index,
extra witnesses, siblings, arguments, an unencodable output, or bytes
moved across a script/argument boundary all get distinct names, none
equal to the valid transaction's identity, and that the name depends on
the chain ID. A fixed vector computed by the test framework matches the
node, and feature_v2_fallback_identity.py checks that testmempoolaccept
and decoderawtransaction report the framework's name for four such
transactions.

owners.subject: v2: add a generic registry of deferred (two-phase) transaction checks
owners.message:
v2: add a generic registry of deferred (two-phase) transaction checks

The per-transaction V2 post-check was one function that knew about
ENFORCEOUTPUT claims and HAS_STATE authorization. The deferred rules will
change as contracts are built, so replace it with a small generic
mechanism (lotus_v2/deferred_checks.h):

- Phase 1: an invocation stages typed records (DeferredRecords) in its
  input's slot. They are merged only when the invocation succeeds, as
  before. A successful input hands its records to every registered kind's
  inline update. Inputs share no mutable state other than these
  order-free accumulators.
- Phase 2: each kind's optional final rule runs once per transaction,
  after every input succeeded. Records are seen by input index, then
  witness index, whatever order the inputs completed in.
- DeferredTxRun schedules this with an atomic count of pending inputs.
  The completion that reaches zero runs the final rules, so no block-wide
  barrier is needed. A failed input marks the transaction failed and its
  records are dropped before any update, so they never reach phase 2.
  Completing an input twice fails closed.
- Optional phase 3: DeferredBlockHook. The consensus registry has none
  yet; RunDeferredBlockChecks is a tested no-op.
- A kind is one record type, one accumulator and one registry entry.
  Nothing in the scheduler changes when a kind is added.

The existing rules become the first two consensus kinds, in canonical
order: state authorization (every HAS_STATE output authorized), then
output claims (for now, unchanged: claims on output j sum to at most its
value). All callers now run them through the same registry:

- ordinary validation;
- CScriptCheck: a shared V2DeferredTxChecks per transaction, completed by
  each input's check;
- VerifyTxScriptsFromResolvedCoins, including its fast path, which uses a
  separate run so a fallback to the general loop starts fresh;
- testv2transaction and the simulation evaluator, through the sequential
  driver RunDeferredChecks;
- the V2 VM fuzz target.

Behaviour is unchanged: V2 transactions are still checked as one unit
in CheckInputScripts, and the reject reasons are the same.

- a test-only dummy kind, registered next to the consensus kinds, with an
  inline upper bound and a final rule;
- sequential, shuffled and thread-per-input completion give the same
  outcome, run the final rules exactly once and see records in canonical
  order;
- inline failures skip phase 2;
- failed inputs' records never reach phase 2;
- double completion fails closed;
- each consensus kind passes and fails, and reject reasons follow
  registry order;
- the block hook.

owners.subject: v2: assign ENFORCEOUTPUT claims by maximum flow; push no output index
owners.message:
v2: assign ENFORCEOUTPUT claims by maximum flow; push no output index

Consensus rule (user, 2026-10-20): a transaction is valid only if every
ENFORCEOUTPUT claim can be assigned to outputs its template matches with
no output receiving more than its value. Before this change, each claim
went to the first matching output and the claims on each output were
summed. That rejected transactions whose claims fit when assigned
differently.

Phase 1 (the opcode). ENFORCEOUTPUT checks its template against every
output in range and records an OutputClaim: the claim amount and the
match mask (every matching output index). A template that matches no
output still fails the invocation. The opcode no longer pushes an output
index, and the size pass no longer models a result. The output_mode byte
is kept: it narrows the mask to one output, as a template constraint.
OUTPUT_FIRST is renamed OUTPUT_ANY to match. A state-constraining
template authorizes every output it matches; each of those carries
exactly the expected root, and under I-10 any extra input could
authorize them anyway.

Phase 2 (the output-claims kind). One maximum-flow feasibility check per
transaction, with no special case for single-match claims:

- graph: source -> each claim (capacity: its amount) -> each output in
  its mask -> sink (capacity: the output value);
- feasible iff the maximum flow equals the total claimed;
- solver: Dinic, with an iterative augmenting search so the depth does
  not depend on the graph size;
- arithmetic: 64-bit edge capacities, 128-bit totals;
- an empty mask or an out-of-range index is rejected inline;
- the reject reason is still "output-overclaimed".

Splitting is the intended semantics (user, 2026-10-21): the flow may
divide one claim's amount among several outputs its template matches, so
several payments can share outputs. Assigning a whole output to one
claim is already expressible with SIGHASH_SINGLE, so the rule does not
restrict it.

Other callers:

- The simulation evaluator records the mask over the current outputs.
  When nothing matches, the constructed draft is the mask. A claim does
  not see outputs that later invocations append.
- testv2transaction and simulatev2transaction report each claim as
  {amount, matches}. post_check.outputs[].claimed is now the flow into
  each output from one maximum flow; other assignments may exist.
- The functional test's vault and creator scripts drop the DROP after
  ENFORCEOUTPUT. A new case spends two payment coins. A first-match rule
  would put both 20k claims on o0 (20k); the flow moves one to o1. The
  transaction is accepted and mined, and a variant with o1 too small is
  rejected with output-overclaimed.

Tests:

- test_lotus_v2_deferred_checks, max-flow cases:
  - a greedy first match fails although an assignment exists;
  - an exhausted output, with another matching output that has room;
  - total and local (Hall) over-claims;
  - overlapping masks on a cycle, at exactly enough room and one unit
    short;
  - a split claim;
  - zero claims;
  - claims at UINT64_MAX with 128-bit totals;
  - the per-output assignment;
  - 3000 random instances checked against the Gale/Hall subset condition.
- test_vm: expected masks instead of indexes, and an empty final stack
  apart from the script's TRUE. The claims block now shows that 60+40+1
  on `any` is feasible, with a pinned claim sharing o1, until the total
  exceeds 300.

owners.subject: v2: run V2 input invocations on the script check queue
owners.message:
v2: run V2 input invocations on the script check queue

Phase 1 of the deferred checks now runs one job per input, in parallel.
Before this change a V2 transaction was a single check unit: its inputs
ran one after another in one worker, and CheckInputScripts refused to
hand V2 checks to pvChecks.

Block connect (pass 2):

- A V2 transaction that needs the VM is split into one CScriptCheck per
  input on the script check queue (CCheckQueue, sized by -par).
- Its checks share a V2DeferredTxChecks, which carries the atomic count
  of pending inputs. The check that completes the last input runs the
  transaction's final rules (phase 2). There is no barrier across the
  block.
- A failed input abandons the transaction, so phase 2 never sees its
  records.
- Each queued input stages its batched signatures in its own collector;
  the collectors are merged after the queue joins.
- Legacy transactions and fast-path V2 spends (single-branch OP_TRUE or
  key-CHECKSIG coins, which stage no records) stay whole on the worker
  pool, which runs while the queue drains.
- The fast-path eligibility test is factored out (GetV2FastPathShape) so
  both sides use the same rule.

Canonical failure reason. When either side fails, the block reports the
first failing transaction in block order:

- pool transactions below the first pool failure have all run;
- a queued transaction that was not accepted is checked again
  sequentially: inputs in order, then the final rules, with a fresh
  per-transaction sigcheck limit and no block limit;
- if nothing fails that way, only the block sigcheck limit was hit, and
  the queue's error is reported.

Block reject reasons now carry the transaction's reason, so a deferred
failure shows up as e.g. output-overclaimed. Script failures have the
same text as before.

The optional per-block hook (RunDeferredBlockChecks) now runs over the
queued transactions' runs in block order. Only queued transactions can
carry records: fast-path scripts stage none, and transactions with
records are never cached.

CheckInputScripts with pvChecks now returns a V2 transaction's per-input
checks and leaves their execution to the caller; the last of them runs
phase 2. Mempool and the RPC paths keep the sequential order (phase 1
then phase 2) through the same kinds.

Script execution cache. A transaction whose inputs staged deferred
records is never inserted, because a cache hit would skip the records
its validity depends on. This applies to CheckInputScripts, the package
and batch path (VerifyTxScriptsFromResolvedCoins reports whether records
were produced) and block pass 2. The validated-ordinary cache of
ordinary_validation follows the same rule: OrdinaryCandidateEffects
carries produced_records, and PutCachedOrdinaryResolved skips marked
candidates.

Tests:

- v2_deferred_block_tests validates the same blocks with -par=1 (no
  script threads) and -par=4, eight times each:
  - a max-flow-feasible claims transaction beside fast-path and
    single-claim transactions;
  - an infeasible one (output-overclaimed);
  - two failing transactions, where the first in block order sets the
    reason;
  - a transaction whose over-claiming input 0 is followed by a failing
    input 1, which reports the script failure (input 1), not the claim.
  The outcomes agree across -par, and the valid block connects. Removing
  the shared deferred state from the queued checks makes the infeasible
  cases pass as valid; the test catches that.
- The same file checks the cache bypass:
  - through CheckInputScripts: a claims transaction is not cached, an
    OP_TRUE one is;
  - after TestBlockValidity (ConnectBlock with fJustCheck, which caches):
    the block's claims transactions are absent from the cache under the
    block's script flags, while the fast-path spend beside them is
    present.
  Dropping either bypass fails its test.
- test_lotus_v2_ordinary_validation: a claims candidate is marked
  produced_records and a plain one is not; a marked candidate put in the
  validated-ordinary cache is not found, an unmarked one is.
- transaction_tests/v2_state_output_post_check now expects one deferred
  check per input, with the final rule running in the last one.

owners.subject: v2: charge ENFORCEOUTPUT a flat cost per output; cap claim pairs per tx
owners.message:
v2: charge ENFORCEOUTPUT a flat cost per output; cap claim pairs per tx

Phase 2 solves one maximum flow per transaction. Its graph has one edge
per (claim, matching output) pair, so the edges are what the cost must
pay for and what the cap bounds.

Cost (user, 2026-10-21): each ENFORCEOUTPUT costs a flat
`per_tx_output x number of transaction outputs`.

- One constant, the new VmOpcodeCost field per_tx_output, replaces
  per_scanned_output.
- The charge does not depend on the output mode or on how many outputs
  match, so the static (consensus) charge and the metered charge are the
  same thing.
- A claim has at most one edge per output, so the charge is at least
  per_tx_output times the claim's edges. It pays for the template scan
  and for the claim's share of phase 2.
- The field is in VmProfileDigest, the ordinary-validation profile
  digest and getv2vmprofile. The node schedule sets it to 32.

Per-transaction cap: MAX_TX_CLAIM_PAIRS = 4096, reported by
getv2vmprofile as limits.max_tx_claim_pairs.

- The output-claims kind keeps an atomic count of pairs. An input whose
  records take the count past the cap fails inline with
  "claim-pairs-exceeded", and so does the transaction.
- The cost does not make the cap redundant. The node consensus path
  limits cost per invocation only (max_invocation_cost = 1,000,000):
  - at 32 x 256 outputs, one invocation can afford about 122
    ENFORCEOUTPUTs, i.e. about 31k edges;
  - a transaction has up to 256 inputs with several witnesses each;
  - there is no per-transaction total in the node path. The ordinary
    path's max_total_invocation_cost is a configured profile value, not
    a consensus bound.
  So the budget gives no per-transaction bound on edges, and inputs
  together could record millions, far past the size phase 2 was
  measured at. The per-transaction cap stays.

Benchmark (bitcoin-bench -filter='V2.*' -min_time=3000; Apple M5 Max,
shared host at load average 26-45, so the numbers are noisy; Release
build):

  V2ClaimFlowLadderAtCap     1186-1375 ns/pair  (4.9-5.6 ms per tx)
  V2ClaimFlowPlantedAtCap      67-85   ns/pair
  V2ClaimFlowCompleteAtCap     14-16   ns/pair
  V2VmCostUnit                 51-59   ns/cost unit

The shapes were found by a wider search over graphs at the transaction
limit of 256 outputs (claims over random 2..16-output masks with a
planted assignment, complete bipartite, single claim, fan-in, and
ladders with steps 1, 2 and 7):

- The slowest was the ladder: claims on adjacent outputs of a chain of
  256, all of them assigned upward, plus one claim on output 0 whose
  room is at the far end. Augmenting paths run along the chain, so Dinic
  needs about one phase per path length, at most 2 x 256.
- Its cost per edge grows with the edge count: 0.7 us at 1024 edges,
  about 1.1-1.4 us at 4096. The total is bounded by roughly
  (2 x outputs) x edges.
- Random sparse graphs at the cap stay below 0.25 us per edge.

Choice:

- Constant. One worst-case edge at the cap costs 22.4-26.8 VM cost
  units of time (ladder ns/pair divided by ns per cost unit, same run).
  The template scan adds under one unit per output, so 32 per output
  covers the worst observed edge with headroom. Below the cap an edge
  is cheaper than at it.
- Cap. 4096 edges keeps the worst phase 2 near 5 ms per transaction;
  the claims that create them pay at least 131,072 units (about 7 ms of
  VM time). The cap is still 16 claims on every one of 256 outputs, or
  4096 single-output claims.

Tests:

- test_lotus_v2_deferred_checks:
  - the cap is reached exactly and crossed, by one input or summed over
    inputs;
  - with concurrent completion the transaction always fails.
- test_vm:
  - a template pinned to one output pays the same flat charge as one
    that may match any output;
  - its static charge equals its executed charge.
- feature_v2_vm_opcodes checks per_tx_output and max_tx_claim_pairs in
  getv2vmprofile.

owners.subject: chronik: native V2 host adapter for native outputs, V2 inputs and identities
owners.message:
chronik: native V2 host adapter for native outputs, V2 inputs and identities

The ABC host adapter converts Lotus V2 node transactions the way the Rust
bridge does:

- Native outputs (empty or one-byte scriptPubKey with branches) are
  indexed as the native output frame flags || value || [token_id] ||
  branches || paths, with implied single-branch paths when none are
  given and no paths for burns, so script groups and responses match.
- Inputs with an empty scriptSig show their coinbase data or the script
  of their first branch witness; non-coinbase mint inputs spend no coin
  and are not indexed (spent coins stay indexed by vin index).
- DecodeRawTx takes the txid from the node's own decoding of the raw
  bytes (design C1 section 1.2) instead of a legacy-shaped recompute.
- Tx sizes are those of the legacy-shaped serialization of the
  converted tx, as the Rust Chronik reports them (TxMut::ser_len), not
  the native V2 wire size.
- SLP/ALP token indexing is off on V2 nodes (user decision 2026-10-19),
  detected by the V2 output fields, and stays on for eCash.

All V2 handling is selected at compile time on the node's transaction
fields. Tests check the frames against the node's lotus::v2::EncodeOutput
and cover V2 input scripts and mint skipping.

burns from outputs and coinbase inputs, in the six legacy-env tables
v2_branch_history[_num_txs], v2_branch_utxo, v2_asset_history[_num_txs]
and v2_asset_utxo (page size 1000, sats as UTXO data).

LegacyGroupsExtension registers the groups inside the core's write txn
and the ws.rs subscriptions: WsSub script types "v2-branch" and
"taproot" (32-byte branch root) and "v2-asset" (32-byte asset ID). The
ABC host passes it on V2 nodes. V2ThreeBranchOutput ports the Rust
helper.

Rust's mempool V2 group indexes are read only by its Electrum server,
which the native implementation does not have, so they are not kept.

owners.message:
chronik: native V2 /v2 and explorer HTTP routes

Port chronik-http v2.rs and v2_explorer.rs onto the native router, served
by the V2 service extension (AbcV2ServiceExtension::RegisterRoutes):

  GET  /v2/status, /v2/utxos/:txid/:out_idx
  POST /v2/branches/utxos, /v2/branches/outputs
  GET  /v2/explorer/v1/{status, blocks, blocks/by-height/:height,

  POST /v2/explorer/v1/branches/{outputs,utxos}

Each request takes the then-current service (index_unavailable while it

fenced by the authority observation, as in Rust. Request and response caps,
status codes, error codes, snapshot tokens and both cursor formats follow
the Rust code. The explorer routes read the raw URI (axum OriginalUri), so
they use raw path extraction.

The JSON layer reproduces serde_json: objects with sorted keys (its
BTreeMap Map), compact output and its string escapes, and a strict parser
with serde derive semantics for the request structs (deny_unknown_fields,
duplicates, defaults, Option fields, struct sequences, integer ranges,
recursion limit, UTF-8 and surrogate checks).

owners.message:
chronik: native V2 index bounds follow the consensus block-size limit

65536-change and 32 MiB staging bounds.

and explorer reads use it. The ABC host passes the configured maximum
block size, at least the 1 GB adaptive ceiling, within 32 bits, and
derives the transaction and change limits from it. Stored records are
unchanged, so DB dumps stay equal to Rust's.

the node's block files"; this commit carries only chronik/native and

The V2 index (Rust chronik-db and native lotus_v2, kept at byte parity)
no longer copies transactions. A tx record stores the transaction's
block-file position; bytes are read back through the node and checked
against the recorded identity, size and checksum.

Records (schema 4, identical postcard layouts in Rust and native):
- eT TxMeta: location, lock, counts, file_num u32, data_pos u32 (was
  u64 into v2_tx_NNNNN.dat), wire_size, wire_checksum (seahash).
- 'b' receipt: (anchor, parent, block facts, [ReceiptTx {location,
  file_num, data_pos, wire_size, wire_checksum}]) instead of full txs.
- coins subdb (was outputs; key 'o'+outpoint): Coin {flags, value,
  token_id iff flags&1, spend: Option<(spender txid, input index)>}.
  The script/branches/paths and the creation location are no longer
  copied; queries that need them read the creating tx through the node.
- eI stores StoredInputMeta without the frozen spent output; the
  public InputMeta.resolved_creation is filled at query time.
- Undo drops the flat-file position.
- The flat files (v2_tx_*.dat) and the outputs table are gone.

ReadTxFromDisk, under the block's own BridgeV2NativeTx conversion;
tests: MemTxSource) loads NodeTx at (file, pos); the index checks txid,
txhash, wire size and seahash and fails closed (Error::Node / Corrupt).
Positions are bindex.nDataPos + header + CompactSize(vtx), advanced by
each tx's serialized size, read under cs_main. Read budgets are
unchanged. Connect resolves spent coins from in-block creations or the
coin record; exact replay compares receipt, explorer entries, coins and
spend refs. Disconnect rebuilds the block from the node and verifies the

primitives(v2): version-tagged transactions without hybrid fields

A transaction is either legacy (version 1 or 2: legacy inputs and outputs
in the eCash grammar, named by SHA256d) or V2 (version 7: V2 inputs and V2
outputs in the v7 grammar). Any other version has no serialization and does
not decode (bad-txns-version). The wrapped 0x80000007/0xC0000007 forms, the
version XOR of legacy identities, the flat fallback identity and
HasStructuralV2Identity are deleted; a version 7 transaction without a
structural identity does not construct (bad-txns-v2-identity).

The CTxIn/CTxOut fields are kept (Chronik reads them); the invariant is
enforced where a transaction gets its bytes, so a mixed transaction cannot
exist. A version 7 output with branches and a scriptPubKey other than its V2
encoding is refused. CMutableTransaction defaults to version 2.

- ToV2Output is lossless: a legacy output maps to legacy_script, so the V2
  state records legacy coins with the 0x80 EncodeCoin record. The implicit
  V0-leaf mapping of legacy scripts is gone; primitives/v2_outputs.h builds
  explicit V2 outputs (V0LeafOutput, OpTrueOutput) and matches coinbase
  payees (CoinbaseOutputPaysScript), used by the miner fund, staking
  rewards and treasury rules.
- TxOutCompression stores a V2 output by its fields (V2 tag) and reads it
  back with its V2 encoding as scriptPubKey; a legacy output by its script.
- The 256-input/256-output caps apply to every version;
  bad-txns-legacy-state-output is deleted (unrepresentable).
- Token extraction and the 45-byte OP_TRUE script path no longer parse
  legacy scriptPubKeys as V2 outputs.

owners.subject: consensus(v2): let v7 spend legacy P2PKH coins with a V2 signature
owners.message:
consensus(v2): let v7 spend legacy P2PKH coins with a V2 signature

A version 7 input (nFlags 1) may spend a coin created by a legacy
transaction when the coin is exactly P2PKH (rules A5/A6, design §2.3):

- Shape (CheckTxInputs): path index 0, one witness without siblings, an
  empty script and arguments [sig, 33-byte compressed pubkey]; else
  bad-txns-v2-legacy-coin-witness. Uncompressed keys are refused (Q3).
  Another legacy script gives bad-txns-v2-legacy-coin-template.
- Key hash (CheckTxInputs): HASH160(pubkey) must be the coin's key hash,
  else bad-txns-v2-legacy-p2pkh.
- Signature (CScriptCheck::CheckLegacyBridgeInput): a V2 BIP340 signature
  (64 bytes, or 65 with mode byte 1 or 2) by the pubkey's x-only key over
  the V2 signing message of invocation (input, witness 0), verified through
  the block's batch collector like any V2 signature.

Signing message for legacy coins (§2.5):
- A coin's wire is EncodeCoinOutput: EncodeOutput for a V2 coin, and
  LegacyCoinWire = 0x80 || value || CompactSize(|script|) || script for a
  legacy coin, the bytes EncodeCoin already records in the state (which
  now uses the same function). The coins root, the own-input hash, the
  coin field sizes and coin introspection (0xdc) use it. EncodeOutput
  still refuses legacy outputs as transaction outputs.
- The selector leaf is LegacyBridgeLeaf = TaggedHash(Branch, 0x03 ||
  CS(coin script) || CS(witness script)), with branch index 0, so a bridge
  signature never verifies for a native V2 spend or another coin.
- The all-OP_TRUE and pure-mode-0 preparation shortcuts are not taken for
  legacy coins.

Tests (v2_legacy_bridge_tests): modes 0/1/2 valid in a block and in the
mempool, the spent coin removed and the new coin V2; the coin stays
spendable by a legacy transaction; wrong key hash; another key's
signature, mislabelled modes, mode bytes 0/3 and a signature for another
transaction fail; every bad witness shape; an uncompressed key; P2PK, OP_TRUE,
bare multisig and P2PKH-plus-opcode coins are not templates; bridge and

block and any one bad signature invalidates it.

owners.message:
consensus(v2): let v7 spend legacy P2SH coins on the legacy interpreter

A version 7 input may spend a legacy P2SH coin (rule A7, design §2.4). The
witness is one witness without siblings on path 0 whose script is the
redeem script and whose arguments are the pushes that precede it in a
legacy scriptSig.

- CheckTxInputs: the coin's script is P2SH (a9 14 <20> 87) or P2PKH, else
  bad-txns-v2-legacy-coin-template; HASH160(redeem script) must be the
  coin's script hash, else bad-txns-v2-legacy-p2sh-hash.
- CScriptCheck: the unchanged legacy VerifyScript runs the coin's script
  with scriptSig' = minimal pushes of the arguments and of the redeem
  script, under the flags a v1/v2 spend gets at the same height (Q4), and
  its sigchecks count toward the same limits. Legacy inputs and P2SH bridge
  inputs share one interpreter routine (RunLegacyScript); only the checker
  and the scriptSig differ. The coin comes from the resolved coins (block
  validation passes no spent output to v7 inputs).
- LegacyBridgeSignatureChecker (script/bridge_checker): CheckSig takes a
  legacy signature (ECDSA DER or 64-byte Schnorr, plus hashtype) over the
  V2 signing message of (input, witness 0) in the mode its hashtype
  selects: 0x41 mode 0, 0xC1 mode 1, 0xC3 mode 2 (Q5); scriptCode does
  not enter the message (the selector leaf commits to the redeem script).
  Verification goes through the input's caching checker, so the
  signature cache and the batch collector apply. CHECKDATASIG is
  unchanged. CheckLockTime compares against the V2 lock (value lock >> 8,
  height or time by its kind byte) and needs a non-final sequence;
  CheckSequence is BIP68 without the version gate.

each mapped hashtype, in a block and in the mempool; hashtypes 0x01, 0x42,
0x43, 0x81 and 0x40, another key, a legacy-sighash signature and a
relabelled mode fail; wrong redeem hash; a P2SH-plus-opcode coin is not a
template; for thirteen signature-free redeem scripts (OP_TRUE, OP_FALSE,

owners.subject: lotus_v2: slab-backed persistent Merklix snapshots with lazy hashing and MinHash
owners.message:
lotus_v2: slab-backed persistent Merklix snapshots with lazy hashing and MinHash

Replace the append-only TxOverlayArena inside every MempoolOverlayLayer with
txmerklix::Tree: a path-compressed, reference-counted persistent tree whose
branch and leaf nodes live in per-family slabs addressed by 32-bit handles.
Exclusively owned (path-unique) nodes are mutated in place; shared nodes are
path-copied. Freed slots are reclaimed in batches and reused with generation
counters; a solely owned empty store returns its chunks. Digests are lazy
derived caches published with a Dirty/Busy/Clean compare-and-swap, so
ordinary readers never hash and any number of threads can complete the
commitment of an immutable pinned version. Consensus Subtree A is unchanged
and equality with TransactionSubtreeA and the legacy arena is tested.

Epoch freezes now share the tree in O(1) and block-connect re-anchoring
adopts the existing trees and cached digests instead of re-inserting every
transaction. The RPC template snapshot pins Subtree A under the mempool lock
and hashes after releasing it.

Full-mempool reconciliation captures pin the mempool's working tree in O(1)
under cs_main and mempool.cs instead of copying every transaction reference
and rebuilding/eagerly hashing a private trie; the legacy rebuild remains as
an explicit fallback and as the bounded page verifier. Each pinned version
carries an incrementally maintained bottom-k (k=64) MinHash of the same
(TxId, TxHash) membership with exact deletion support (candidate buffer of
256 with lazy bounded rebuild). Scope-5 frames are version 2: offers carry
the sketch, receivers record Jaccard/remote-only estimates and their error
against the authenticated traversal. The sketch is a hint only and never
decides fetching, validity or finality. Prometheus exposes txmerklix and
fullrecon series.

The RPC entry radix index, UTXO SMT/overlay and short-id relay index are
unchanged. Specification: daemon/docs/slab-merklix-snapshots-spec.md in the
monorepo.
